inputs.original_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened sincerely held religious beliefs. That turns religious freedom into a tool for preserving abortion access, while sidelining the state’s responsibility to defend unborn life. The real question is not whether one side’s moral convictions count: it is whether those convictions should override protections for the most vulnerable. LifeNews’ phrase “killing babies” is blunt, but it reflects the moral stakes rather than settling the debate by calling concern for unborn life mere stigma.
inputs.modified_text: This ruling shows how religious liberty can be repurposed to protect abortion access while the state’s duty to defend unborn life is pushed aside. Conscience matters, but it cannot automatically settle the question when the lives of the most vulnerable are at stake. Calling the practice “killing babies” is harsh; it is also a way of insisting that the moral reality not be softened into mere stigma.
